title: Palindrome check
question: Check a palindrome ignoring case and punctuation.
answer: const isPalindrome = s => { const t=s.toLowerCase().replace(/[^a-z0-9]/g,''); return t===[...t].reverse().join(''); };
explanation: Normalize before comparing with the reverse. This example treats ASCII letters and digits as significant.

title: Character frequency
question: Count each character in a string.
answer: const charFrequency = s => { const m=new Map(); for(const c of s)m.set(c,(m.get(c)||0)+1); return Object.fromEntries(m); };
explanation: Map stores counts without ordinary-object prototype key collisions.

title: First non-repeating character
question: Find the first character occurring once, or null.
answer: function firstUnique(s){const m=new Map(); for(const c of s)m.set(c,(m.get(c)||0)+1); for(const c of s)if(m.get(c)===1)return c; return null;}
explanation: Count first, then scan again to preserve original order.

title: Anagram check
question: Check if two strings are anagrams ignoring case and whitespace.
explanation: Normalize and compare sorted characters. A frequency map can improve asymptotic time.

title: Remove duplicates
question: Remove duplicate array values preserving order.
explanation: Set preserves insertion order and uniqueness by JavaScript value identity rules.

title: Flatten nested array
question: Flatten any nesting level in an array.
explanation: flat returns a new array and does not mutate the source.

title: Second largest distinct number
question: Find second-largest distinct number or null.
answer: function secondLargest(a){let max=-Infinity,second=-Infinity; for(const n of a){if(n>max){second=max;max=n;}else if(n<max&&n>second)second=n;} return second===-Infinity?null:second;}
explanation: One pass tracks two distinct maxima; assumes finite numeric inputs.

title: Find missing number
question: Find missing value from range 0..n with one missing.
answer: function missingNumber(a){let r=a.length; for(let i=0;i<a.length;i++)r+=i-a[i]; return r;}
explanation: Expected sum minus actual sum, computed in a loop.

title: Two Sum
question: Return indices of two numbers adding to target.
answer: function twoSum(a,target){const seen=new Map(); for(let i=0;i<a.length;i++){const need=target-a[i]; if(seen.has(need))return [seen.get(need),i]; seen.set(a[i],i);} return [];}
explanation: A map stores previously seen values; check before inserting the current item.

title: Merge sorted arrays
question: Merge two sorted arrays.
explanation: Two pointers choose the next smallest value; inputs must be sorted ascending.

title: Rotate array right
question: Rotate an array right by k positions.
explanation: Modulo handles large and negative rotations. Returns a new array.

title: Group objects by property
question: Group records by a property key.
explanation: reduce builds arrays under each property value. Use Map if keys are arbitrary objects or untrusted special strings.

title: Deep clone JSON data

title: Debounce
question: Implement debounce: call after invocations stop for delay.
explanation: Each call cancels the prior timer and uses the latest arguments and context.

title: Throttle
question: Implement leading-edge throttle.
explanation: Drops calls during the wait window; it does not schedule a trailing call.

title: Memoize unary function
question: Cache results for a pure function of one argument.
answer: function memoize(fn){const cache=new Map();return function(x){if(cache.has(x))return cache.get(x);const y=fn.call(this,x);cache.set(x,y);return y;};}
explanation: Map.has distinguishes cached undefined from absent entries. Add an eviction policy for unbounded workloads.

title: Closure counter
question: Create a counter whose state persists between calls.
explanation: Returned methods close over the private local variable.

title: Custom reduce
question: Implement reduce with an optional initial value.
answer: function customReduce(a,fn,...initial){let i=0,acc;if(initial.length)acc=initial[0];else{while(i<a.length&&!(i in a))i++;if(i===a.length)throw new TypeError('Reduce of empty array');acc=a[i++];}for(;i<a.length;i++)if(i in a)acc=fn(acc,a[i],i,a);return acc;}
explanation: Handles empty input, optional initial value, and sparse holes for the common reduce behavior.

title: Binary search
question: Find target index in a sorted array, or -1.
explanation: Requires ascending sorted input and returns any matching index if duplicates exist.

title: Maximum subarray sum
question: Find the maximum sum of a non-empty contiguous subarray.
explanation: Kadane's algorithm either starts at the current value or extends the prior subarray; works with all-negative arrays.

title: Pair sum in sorted array
question: Find two values adding to target in a sorted array.
answer: function pairSumSorted(a,target){let l=0,r=a.length-1;while(l<r){const s=a[l]+a[r];if(s===target)return [a[l],a[r]];if(s<target)l++;else r--;}return null;}
explanation: Two pointers work because the input is sorted ascending.

title: Balanced brackets
question: Check if (), [] and {} are balanced.
answer: function isBalanced(s){const pairs={')':'(',']':'[','}':'{'};const stack=[];for(const c of s){if('([{'.includes(c))stack.push(c);else if(')]}'.includes(c)&&stack.pop()!==pairs[c])return false;}return stack.length===0;}
explanation: Each closing bracket must match the most recent opening bracket. Other characters are ignored.

title: Stack class
question: Implement stack push, pop, peek and isEmpty.
explanation: Private class fields protect the internal array; pop/peek return undefined when empty.

title: Queue using two stacks
question: Implement enqueue and dequeue with two stacks.
explanation: Transfer only when output stack is empty. Each element moves at most once between stacks.

title: Fibonacci with BigInt
question: Return nth Fibonacci number exactly.
answer: function fibonacci(n){if(!Number.isInteger(n)||n<0)throw new RangeError('n must be non-negative');let a=0n,b=1n;for(let i=0;i<n;i++)[a,b]=[b,a+b];return a;}
explanation: BigInt preserves exact integer results; F(0)=0 and F(1)=1.

title: Promise.all implementation
question: Implement a simplified Promise.all preserving input order.
answer: function promiseAll(iterable){return new Promise((resolve,reject)=>{const items=Array.from(iterable);if(!items.length)return resolve([]);const out=new Array(items.length);let done=0;items.forEach((item,i)=>Promise.resolve(item).then(v=>{out[i]=v;if(++done===items.length)resolve(out);},reject));});}
explanation: Assimilates promises and values and rejects on first rejection. Prefer native Promise.all in application code.

title: Run async tasks sequentially
question: Run async task functions one after another and collect results.
answer: async function runSequentially(tasks){const results=[];for(const task of tasks)results.push(await task());return results;}
explanation: Await in the loop enforces sequential execution; use Promise.all for independent tasks that may run concurrently.

title: Retry async operation
question: Retry an async function up to a maximum number of attempts.
answer: async function retry(fn,attempts=3){if(attempts<1)throw new RangeError('attempts must be positive');let error;for(let i=0;i<attempts;i++){try{return await fn();}catch(e){error=e;if(i===attempts-1)throw error;}}}
explanation: Retries can help transient failures. Production code may need backoff, jitter, cancellation, and idempotency.

title: Promise timeout
question: Reject if a promise does not settle before a timeout.
answer: function withTimeout(promise,ms){let timer;const timeout=new Promise((_,reject)=>{timer=setTimeout(()=>reject(new Error('Timed out')),ms);});return Promise.race([promise,timeout]).finally(()=>clearTimeout(timer));}
explanation: Promise.race does not cancel the underlying operation; use AbortController when the API supports cancellation.

title: Fetch JSON with error handling
question: Fetch JSON and throw for non-2xx HTTP responses.
answer: async function fetchJson(url){const res=await fetch(url);if(!res.ok)throw new Error(`HTTP ${res.status}`);return res.json();}
explanation: fetch rejects on network errors but not automatically on HTTP 404/500; check response.ok.

title: Limit async concurrency
question: Map items with a maximum number of concurrent async tasks.
answer: async function mapLimit(items,limit,mapper){if(!Number.isInteger(limit)||limit<1)throw new RangeError('limit must be positive');const out=new Array(items.length);let next=0;async function worker(){while(true){const i=next++;if(i>=items.length)return;out[i]=await mapper(items[i],i);}}await Promise.all(Array.from({length:Math.min(limit,items.length)},worker));return out;}
explanation: Workers claim indexes before awaiting, limiting in-flight operations and preserving output order.

title: Parse query string
question: Parse query parameters and collect repeated keys into arrays.
answer: function parseQuery(q){const out={};for(const [k,v] of new URLSearchParams(q.startsWith('?')?q.slice(1):q)){if(Object.hasOwn(out,k))out[k]=Array.isArray(out[k])?[...out[k],v]:[out[k],v];else out[k]=v;}return out;}
explanation: URLSearchParams handles percent encoding; repeated keys become arrays.

title: LRU cache
question: Implement an LRU cache with get and put using Map order.
answer: class LRUCache{constructor(capacity){if(capacity<1)throw new RangeError('capacity must be positive');this.capacity=capacity;this.map=new Map();}get(k){if(!this.map.has(k))return undefined;const v=this.map.get(k);this.map.delete(k);this.map.set(k,v);return v;}put(k,v){this.map.delete(k);this.map.set(k,v);if(this.map.size>this.capacity)this.map.delete(this.map.keys().next().value);}}
explanation: Refreshing insertion order marks a key most-recently-used; the first key is evicted as least-recently-used.

title: Inorder tree traversal
question: Return inorder traversal of a binary tree.
explanation: Visits left subtree, node, then right subtree. A BST yields sorted values.

title: Binary tree height
question: Return the number of nodes on the longest root-to-leaf path.
explanation: The empty tree height is defined as zero; recursion depth depends on tree height.

title: Breadth-first graph search
question: Return BFS visit order using an adjacency-list object.
answer: function bfs(graph,start){const seen=new Set([start]),queue=[start],order=[];for(let i=0;i<queue.length;i++){const node=queue[i];order.push(node);for(const next of graph[node]||[])if(!seen.has(next)){seen.add(next);queue.push(next);}}return order;}
explanation: Mark nodes visited when enqueuing them to avoid duplicates. Map is better for arbitrary node keys.

title: Merge overlapping intervals
question: Merge overlapping [start,end] intervals.
answer: function mergeIntervals(intervals){const sorted=intervals.map(x=>[...x]).sort((a,b)=>a[0]-b[0]),out=[];for(const cur of sorted){const last=out.at(-1);if(!last||cur[0]>last[1])out.push(cur);else last[1]=Math.max(last[1],cur[1]);}return out;}
explanation: Sort by start, then extend the previous interval if they overlap. Copies input pairs to avoid mutation.

title: Safe JSON parse
question: Parse JSON and return a fallback on malformed input.
explanation: Use a fallback only when silently recovering from malformed data is appropriate; otherwise report the parsing error.

title: Optional chaining and nullish coalescing
question: Read nested city safely and default only for null or undefined.
explanation: Optional chaining avoids errors on nullish intermediates; ?? preserves valid falsy values such as empty strings and zero.

title: Sleep with Promise
question: Create a Promise-based sleep helper.
answer: const sleep = ms => new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, ms));
explanation: Timer execution happens after at least the requested delay and can be delayed by event-loop load.
